candidates.lead: Jacinta Bathalda says she was horrified to see her car get stolen but was determined to get it back
candidates.evidence_text: How a Salford woman tracked her stolen Audi with an app - BBC News Image caption, Jacinta Bathalda did not know her car had a tracker Published 33 minutes ago By Paul Burnell North West A woman who traced and retrieved her stolen £40,000 car has said she fears reprisals from the thief but is glad she did it. Mother-of-four Jacinta Bathalda, 35, from Little Hulton, Salford, was awoken at 03:00 BST on 10 August by her son's shouts and was horrified to see someone stealing her car. Sceptical when the police told her they were looking for the vehicle, she was inspired to search for it herself when a friend asked if the Audi had a tracker. Greater Manchester Police (GMP) has been contacted for a comment. Bathalda said: "I worked hard to pay this for this car, so I was upset when I just saw a stranger take it." She was alerted to the manufacturer's app by a friend who worked for Audi, and was amazed five days after the theft when it informed her the car was low on petrol. She and her family then drove to an address 30 miles away in Blackburn, where the app said the car was. Image source, CCTV Image caption, Jacinta Bathalda obtained CCTV of her car black in east Lancashire At first she drew a blank, but after asking round in the neighbourhood one person sent her a video of her car with new number plates fitted. "I was so shocked," Bathalda said, adding a DVLA check revealed the plates were for a Volkswagen. Later that day, the app revealed another location 20 minutes away in Colne, where she saw the car and recognised her belongings inside. She got inside and decided to drive off in case the thief returned to it. She said she then called the police, who said she should have contacted them first to prevent the contamination of fingerprint evidence. Bathalda alleged there was little follow-up from GMP. When asked of the repercussions of being her own detective, she said: "To be honest, I'm not scared of these guys. "I don't know if they're going to come, if they're going to try to recover the car again, because they still have the key. "I sleep one hour a day because I always watch my camera to see if they can come again." candidates.lead: International singers including Ariana Grande and Nelly Furtado have performed at Manchester Pride
candidates.evidence_text: How Manchester Pride evolved from a bring-and-buy sale - BBC News Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Pride in Manchester began in 1985 from very humble beginnings By Darren Milby Radio Manchester Published 36 minutes ago Manchester Village Pride may look and feel familiar this year but a lot has changed over the past 12 months. The annual event, held over the August bank holiday weekend, hit the headlines in October 2025 when the company behind it went into voluntary administration. Manchester Pride Events LTD owed more than £1m to suppliers and performers. Many of these have still not been paid and the Charity Commission has launched an investigation into the organisation's finances. But how did Manchester Pride reach this point and what does the future hold? Pride in Manchester began in 1985 from very humble beginnings and grew into one of Europe's largest LGBTQ+ festivals attracting more than 170,000 visitors. Big names from the pop world such as Ariana Grande and Nelly Furtado have graced the stage and huge corporate brands were queuing up to have their logos associated with the weekend-long event. This is a world away from the very first Manchester Pride. Image source, Stuart Rhoades Image caption, For more than 40 years, people have gathered in Manchester for the annual event It started with a bring-and-buy sale on Canal Street in the city's Gay Village in 1985. The aim was to raise funds for the ward at Monsall Hospital in north Manchester that was treating patients at the height of the HIV and Aids crisis. The ward looked drab and depressing so fundraisers used the money raised to transform the unit into a welcoming space for patients and their families. From these humble beginnings, Manchester Pride started to evolve. There was also a commercial reason for choosing the August bank holiday weekend. "Everybody in Manchester went over to Blackpool for the August bank holiday weekend," said Paul Martin, chief executive of the charity LGBT Foundation. "It's a knockout...all sorts of games like that were an enticement to drag people back to Manchester." Since that first event more than 40 years ago, Pride has always been held on the August bank holiday weekend. The timing may have remained consistent, but the name has changed over the years. It has been called Tickled Pink, as well as Mardi Gras, and The Carnival of Fun. It was simply known as Manchester Pride for the last few years and this summer it will be Manchester Village Pride. Image source, Stuart Rhoades Image caption, Julian Clary, pictured on stage at Manchester Pride in 1994 By the 1990s, the event was established and growing. The Village Charity was set up and Manchester Mardi Gras - The Carnival of Fun became the latest incarnation and, for the first time, the event stretched over the whole bank holiday weekend. Manchester is renowned across the world for its LGBTQ+ scene. One of the reasons for its success was the Gay Village situated around Canal Street. This dates back to the time when homosexuality was illegal. Gay men faced legal penalties and social shame, but those quiet, dimly lit canal-side streets became a discrete place to meet up. The first dedicated venue, The New Union Hotel, which is still open today, provided a safe space for the community. Gradually more venues sprung up in the area and the Gay Village was born. Image source, Stuart Rhoades Image caption, Manchester became one of the biggest Pride events in the UK, alongside London and Brighton's annual celebrations In 1990 a new bar opened in the Gay Village called Manto, meaning Manchester Tomorrow. This venue, which is now called On Bar, was not hidden away and discreet. It stood proud with large windows and balconies and showed that LGBTQ+ party goers no longer needed to hide away in dingy little bars. Manchester's Canal Street started to become a popular destination. This was partly fuelled by the 1999 Russel T. Davies drama Queer as Folk, which centred around life on Canal Street and showed a side of the gay community rarely represented in the media. Such was the draw of a Pride in Manchester's Gay Village, thousands of visitors flocked from all over and new measures were needed. Pride Before the Fall Across the country Prides are smaller, less corporate and in some cases just cancelled altogether Listen on Sounds In 1999 Manchester City Council took over the reins and introduced barriers around the Gay Village and attendees were charged an entrance fee. candidates.lead: Known as the Queen of Crime, her murder mysteries have captivated audiences for more than a century
candidates.evidence_text: The country house in Cheadle that inspired Agatha Christie's work - BBC News Image caption, Agatha Christie wrote 78 crime novels that have sold an estimated 2 billion copies in 44 languages By Jen Dale BBC Radio Manchester Published 22 August 2026 Known as the Queen of Crime, Agatha Christie murder mysteries have captivated audiences for more than a century. But it might come as a surprise to some that many of her stories were inspired by a country house in Cheadle, Greater Manchester. Abney Hall is the subject of a new episode of Hidden Manchester on BBC Sounds after the Cheadle Civic Society erected an information board in the grounds explaining the novelist's connections. In 1902, Christie first arrived at Abney Hall when she was about 11 years old as her older sister Madge lived at the house after marrying into the wealthy Watts family. Nestled in the village of Cheadle, the gothic building has high-ceilinged rooms, gold chandeliers and a red velvet carpet running down the centre of a large wooden staircase. Outside, there are crosses etched into the stone walls as well as distinctive chimney stacks - no doubt the inspiration for one of her stories The Secret of Chimneys. Image source, Cheadle Civic Society Image caption, Abney Hall and the surrounding gardens forms part of a new heritage trail Trever Evers, from the society, said there were plenty of features to inspire the writer. "You know Abney Hall had it all, it had a waterfall, it had a tunnel under the drive," he said. "She loved the fact that the house had back passageways and staircases that they used to hide from each other." Evers added that the geography of Abney Hall was itself an inspiration. "The 4.50 from Paddington [was] a very famous Miss Marple novel," he said. "That's inspired by the grounds at Abney because in Agatha's day the estate was probably I think 10 times bigger than we know it today and the grounds were circled by two railway lines. "The plot revolves around a murder that happens on a train and the body gets pushed out of the train into the estate of a country house. "The fact that Abney was surrounded by these two railway lines, one of which does curve which forces trains to slow down, that is said to have inspired the storyline for that." How Cheadle's Abney Hall inspired Agatha Christie The country house inspired plots in several of her stories Listen on Sounds However, it was in 1926 that Abney Hall plays its most crucial role for Christie. On 3 December of that year, she famously went missing. It was shortly after her successful novel - The murder of Roger Akroyd - had been published. Whilst there were unproved rumours it was to boost book sales, her grandson Matthew Pritchard told the BBC in 2015 there was a lot going on in her life at that time. "I do fairly strongly believe that what she suffered from is rooted in deep unhappiness," he said. "This all that happened when her husband was in the process of leaving her but her mother died and suddenly her whole world crashed from beneath her. "It can provide unexpected effects on your health and maybe an unconscious desire to go away somewhere and wish you weren't there." Image source, Cheadle Civic Society Image caption, The information board about Agatha Christie is part of the new Cheadle heritage trail The search for Christie was one of the largest in the history of Surrey police. She was found 11 days later more than 200 miles away at a hotel in Harrogate. Her sister Madge went to collect her and brought her back to Abney Hall to recover. Evers said the whole episode was a media frenzy at the time. Christie stayed at the country house over the Christmas period of 1926 to recuperate. She went on to write many more books featuring the detectives Hercule Poirot and Miss Marple, who is named after the local train station. To play this video you need to enable JavaScript in your browser. This video can not be played Figure caption, Cheadle's Abney Hall inspired Agatha Christie Christie died in 1976 at the age of 85, having written more than 80 books. Abney Hall stayed in the Watts family for several generations before being sold and became a town hall. It is now leased as office space but the public can access the gardens anytime. The hall is accessible on heritage open days and forms part of the Cheadle heritage trail. candidates.lead: We look at the impact the impact of Manchester Airport's second runway 25 years since opening
candidates.evidence_text: Protests and profits: 25 Years of Manchester's second runway - BBC News Image source, Manchester Airport Image caption, The second runway became operational in 2001 By Judy Hobson , North West Tonight and Jenny Coleman , North West Published 22 August 2026 When Manchester Airport was given permission to build a second runway in 1997 it prompted one of the country's most high-profile environmental protests of the time. Activists from across the country set up camp, built tree houses and a complex network of tunnels in a bid to stop the bulldozers, but after a stand off lasting months they were ultimately evicted and the runway was built. It became operational in 2001 and became the only airport outside of London with two full length runways. Now 25 years on, we look back at the controversy of the project, the impact it has had on the region and its plans for the future. Image source, Manchester Airport Image caption, The airport serves over 32m people each year and connects to more than 200 destinations What were the protests about? Large areas of woodland near to the airport would be need to be removed for the runway to be built. After the plans were approved environmental protesters arrived at the site and set up multiple camps. One of the protestors, Martin Porter who was 27 at the time, was among those that dug tunnels at the site. The protesters were soon joined by a environmental activist named Swampy, real name Dan Hooper. "All the time we were there we had the media, we had Swampy, we were able to give our message that this is a terrible idea, 400 acres of green belt disappearing," Porter said. After six months the group were finally evicted. Local resident, Jeff Gazzard, who was also among the protesters, said the national media attention helped to bring environmental issues into the mainstream. "Climate change began to be an issue then, but it wasn't the headlines it is today," he said. "A lot of things have changed in terms of our understanding of the environmental impact of a major airport." Image caption, Martin Porter, aged 27 at the time, dug tunnels during the protests What benefits has the second runway brought? Supporters at the time argued the airport expansion would bring much needed jobs, attract investment, increase tourism, and strengthen Manchester's position internationally. Fast forward 25 years and a report published this week by the Manchester Airports Group (MAG) claims it has done just that. Damian Woolfenden, 18, is accused of posting Christchurch attacker Brenton Tarrant's live-streamed video of the 2019 killings on to the self-described "pro-white" platform White Pilled TV Woolfenden, formerly of Bury, Greater Manchester, also allegedly posted the manifesto of far-right terrorist Andres Breivik, who killed 77 people in two attacks in Norway on June 22 2011, on to a Telegram group, the court heard He appeared at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Friday via video link, and spoke only to confirm his name and date of birth Woolfenden has been remanded in custody and will next appear at the Old Bailey on 25 September He is said to have had on his home computer the manifesto of US white supremacist mass shooter Payton Gendron and German neo-Nazi synagogue shooter Stephan Balliet along with a firearms guide The teenager is charged with three counts of publishing threatening writ

While they didn't take part in the attack, they accepted being in possession of weapons during the melee Also behind bars this week is thug Courtney Ambrose Lee who attacked two women in a serious of 'utterly terrifying' attacks, and three members of a gang who ran drugs lines named after characters from Sonic the Hedgehog Prison terms are handed out to the worst offenders each week. candidates.evidence_text: True crime series I was alone with an infamous cop killer - I still think about what he did next Retired police officer, Tony Davies, came face to face with Anthony Hughes, who soon after executed Inspector Raymond Codling at Birch Services on the M62 News Lee Grimsditch Features Writer 17:05, 22 Aug 2026 Updated 17:31, 22 Aug 2026 For Tony Davies, it seemed like a routine callout as a police officer in North Wales. He had joined the force at 19 after an unhappy two-year stint in the Merchant Navy But becoming a police officer was different. Working the thin blue line suited him – or, as Tony puts it, he was a "round peg" who found a "round hole". Now 72 and long-retired, he joined the force in the early 1970s and eventually worked his way up to sergeant In the late summer of 1989, Tony found himself heading out to a crime scene after his station in Flintshire received the call about a stolen firearm. "I got called to somebody that nicked a shotgun from the back of a car, and some cartridges, and ran off into the woods," he told After witnesses told him which way the thief had fled, he followed the trail through the woodland until he spotted a figure "There's this guy sitting on a stile, and he's got the gun over his knee and a box of cartridges next to him. I thought, 'There's no way.'

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Crime Constance Marten given permission to appeal sentence for killing her baby girl The aristocrat was jailed for 14 alongside her convicted rapist partner Mark Gordon News PA and Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter 13:19, 22 Aug 2026 View Constance Marten has been granted permission to appeal the 14-year jail sentence she was handed for her baby daughter's death The 39-year-old aristocrat and her convicted rapist partner Mark Gordon, 52, were in hiding when their baby daughter, Victoria, died in a tent on the South Downs in January 2023. The police hunt for the couple began on the M61 motorway near Bolton , when their burning car was dis The defendants had fled authorities to prevent baby Victoria being taken into care, as four other siblings had been before, the Old Bailey had heard. They were found guilty of her manslaughter, child cruelty, concealing the birth of a child and perverting the course of justice fo In September 2025, Judge Mark Lucraft KC jailed them both for 14 years and handed Gordon a further four years on extended licence. The judge accepted the prosecution case that baby Victoria died from hypothermia after being exposed to 'significant cold stress' He rejected the defendants’ claims that Victoria was smothered in a 'terrible accident' as they slept in the tent. The offending was made worse because the baby was vulnerable and the defendants failed to listen to past warnings

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Airport Manchester Airport passengers speak out amid diversions and delays following security breach Seven flights were diverted and at least 17 were held after a man got onto the runway overnight News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news r Passengers have spoken of their experiences of being caught up in flight disruption at Manchester Airport after seven flights were diverted and at least 17 others were held in the skies after a man got onto the airfield Travellers have described how their flights were diverted to East Midlands and Birmingham Airports. One passenger who landed shortly after the incident has praised airport staff on how they ‘seamlessly’ handled the situation Shortly after 11.20pm last night, Friday August 21, police were called to the airport after the man 'encroached' onto the airfield. The incident lasted for around 15 minutes, a spokesperson for Manchester Airport said, before he was taken to hospital from the scene It is understood the incident was mental health-related. The airport spokesperson confirmed the incident was resolved with flights now back to normal. A temporary fix has been put in place following the security breach Among the seven flights diverted were a TUI flight from Boa Vista in Cape Verde, which according to Flightradar24 had to be diverted to East Midlands, a Ryanair flight from Agadir in Morocco diverted to Birmingham and an easyJet flight from Barcelona diverted to Liverpool. candidates.evidence_text: Courts The criminals jailed in Greater Manchester this week - full details of each case The Manchester Evening News has looked back on the cases before our regions courts this week Comments News Andrew Bardsley and Amy Walker Court reporter 20:20, 22 Four Portuguese nationals jailed for their parts in a revenge attack on a 16-year-old boy are among the criminals locked up in Greater Manchester this week It came after two rival gangs in Manchester, comprising of 21 young men, clashed on the streets of Moston on November 5, 2020. Alexander John Soyoye, known as John, was killed brutally stabbed 15 times before he died in the street Ruben Candiza, Valdo De-Almeida, Marco Veiga, and Emerson Teta were this week jailed after pleading guilty to manslaughter. While they didn't take part in the attack, they accepted being in possession of weapons during the melee Also behind bars this week is thug Courtney Ambrose Lee who attacked two women in a serious of 'utterly terrifying' attacks, and three members of a gang who ran drugs lines named after characters from Sonic the Hedgehog Prison terms are handed out to the worst offenders each week. Manchester Evening News reporters are on hand to cover the most serious cases day-in-day-out

candidates.evidence_text: National news Victims to get power to draw up exclusion zones for released prisoners under new crackdown 'No victim should fear the shadow of an abuser on their back' Comments News Alexander Brown and Paul Britton Reporter 19:19, 22 Aug 2026 View 2 Im Serious sexual and violent offenders could be confined to small areas just a few miles wide on their release from prison, it's been revealed In a new crackdown, ministers will bring in strict curbs to the freedoms of offenders, with victims having a say in setting the boundaries in which they must stay The move is said to offer victims greater freedom to travel without the fear of unexpectedly coming face-to-face with their offender However, the zones will also ensure offenders can still access vital appointments and services that help to reduce their chances of reoffending The rollout starts in October, and will see GPS monitoring used to track their movements tracked around the clock, allowing probation services to identify breaches and take swift action when the rules are broken - including recalling them to prison

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Piccadilly Gardens revamp and hundreds of flats amongst latest Greater Manchester developments These are the latest significant developments tabled with councils across Greater Manchster Comments News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporter An overhaul of Piccadilly Gardens and hundreds of new flats for the city centre are just two of the latest developments tabled in Greater Manchester Piccadilly Gardens has long been a talking point amongst city dwellers. In the beating heart of Manchester, the area acts as a transport hub, lunchtime eating spot and a place to hang about Now there are plans to give it a complete makeover. The council intends to make it a ‘distinctive green heart’ Elsewhere in the city centre, Gary Neville ’s property company has joined onto a plan to build more than 700 flats. This scheme, on Great Ancoats Street, would see 723 flats spread over two apartment blocks, if approved Here is a breakdown of each borough’s recently submitted public notices…

candidates.evidence_text: True crime series I was alone with an infamous cop killer - I still think about what he did next Retired police officer, Tony Davies, came face to face with Anthony Hughes, who soon after executed Inspector Raymond Codling at Birch Services on the M62 News Lee Grimsditch Features Writer 17:05, 22 Aug 2026 Updated 17:31, 22 Aug 2026 For Tony Davies, it seemed like a routine callout as a police officer in North Wales. He had joined the force at 19 after an unhappy two-year stint in the Merchant Navy But becoming a police officer was different. Working the thin blue line suited him – or, as Tony puts it, he was a "round peg" who found a "round hole". Now 72 and long-retired, he joined the force in the early 1970s and eventually worked his way up to sergeant In the late summer of 1989, Tony found himself heading out to a crime scene after his station in Flintshire received the call about a stolen firearm. "I got called to somebody that nicked a shotgun from the back of a car, and some cartridges, and ran off into the woods," he told After witnesses told him which way the thief had fled, he followed the trail through the woodland until he spotted a figure "There's this guy sitting on a stile, and he's got the gun over his knee and a box of cartridges next to him. I thought, 'There's no way.'

candidates.evidence_text: Crime Constance Marten given permission to appeal sentence for killing her baby girl The aristocrat was jailed for 14 alongside her convicted rapist partner Mark Gordon News PA and Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter 13:19, 22 Aug 2026 View Constance Marten has been granted permission to appeal the 14-year jail sentence she was handed for her baby daughter's death The 39-year-old aristocrat and her convicted rapist partner Mark Gordon, 52, were in hiding when their baby daughter, Victoria, died in a tent on the South Downs in January 2023. The police hunt for the couple began on the M61 motorway near Bolton , when their burning car was dis The defendants had fled authorities to prevent baby Victoria being taken into care, as four other siblings had been before, the Old Bailey had heard. They were found guilty of her manslaughter, child cruelty, concealing the birth of a child and perverting the course of justice fo In September 2025, Judge Mark Lucraft KC jailed them both for 14 years and handed Gordon a further four years on extended licence. The judge accepted the prosecution case that baby Victoria died from hypothermia after being exposed to 'significant cold stress' He rejected the defendants’ claims that Victoria was smothered in a 'terrible accident' as they slept in the tent. The offending was made worse because the baby was vulnerable and the defendants failed to listen to past warnings

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Airport Manchester Airport passengers speak out amid diversions and delays following security breach Seven flights were diverted and at least 17 were held after a man got onto the runway overnight News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news r Passengers have spoken of their experiences of being caught up in flight disruption at Manchester Airport after seven flights were diverted and at least 17 others were held in the skies after a man got onto the airfield Travellers have described how their flights were diverted to East Midlands and Birmingham Airports. One passenger who landed shortly after the incident has praised airport staff on how they ‘seamlessly’ handled the situation Shortly after 11.20pm last night, Friday August 21, police were called to the airport after the man 'encroached' onto the airfield. The incident lasted for around 15 minutes, a spokesperson for Manchester Airport said, before he was taken to hospital from the scene It is understood the incident was mental health-related. The airport spokesperson confirmed the incident was resolved with flights now back to normal. A temporary fix has been put in place following the security breach Among the seven flights diverted were a TUI flight from Boa Vista in Cape Verde, which according to Flightradar24 had to be diverted to East Midlands, a Ryanair flight from Agadir in Morocco diverted to Birmingham and an easyJet flight from Barcelona diverted to Liverpool. candidates.evidence_text: Crime Six murder probes in two weeks in Greater Manchester - all we know now and what's still to be answered Greater Manchester Police launched murder investigations following deaths in Bolton, Tameside, Rochdale, Salford and Manchester View 7 Images News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter 07:13, 23 Aug 2026 In the space of less than two weeks, six murder investigations were launched in Greater Manchester Two women and four men lost their lives. They all leave behind loved ones, some of them leave behind children Across each of the cases, four men and two women were arrested on suspicion of murder. Some have been charged, some have been bailed. In one of the cases, police later ruled out murder as a line of enquiry The incidents happened in Bolton, Tameside, Rochdale, Salford and Manchester. There is no suggestion that any of the cases are linked The Manchester Evening News has reported in depth on each murder investigation over the past two weeks. Take a look at all we know now about each case, and what is yet to be answered, in our report below

candidates.evidence_text: Courts The criminals jailed in Greater Manchester this week - full details of each case The Manchester Evening News has looked back on the cases before our regions courts this week Comments News Andrew Bardsley and Amy Walker Court reporter 20:20, 22 Four Portuguese nationals jailed for their parts in a revenge attack on a 16-year-old boy are among the criminals locked up in Greater Manchester this week It came after two rival gangs in Manchester, comprising of 21 young men, clashed on the streets of Moston on November 5, 2020. Alexander John Soyoye, known as John, was killed brutally stabbed 15 times before he died in the street Ruben Candiza, Valdo De-Almeida, Marco Veiga, and Emerson Teta were this week jailed after pleading guilty to manslaughter. While they didn't take part in the attack, they accepted being in possession of weapons during the melee Also behind bars this week is thug Courtney Ambrose Lee who attacked two women in a serious of 'utterly terrifying' attacks, and three members of a gang who ran drugs lines named after characters from Sonic the Hedgehog Prison terms are handed out to the worst offenders each week. Manchester Evening News reporters are on hand to cover the most serious cases day-in-day-out

candidates.evidence_text: National news Victims to get power to draw up exclusion zones for released prisoners under new crackdown 'No victim should fear the shadow of an abuser on their back' Comments News Alexander Brown and Paul Britton Reporter 19:19, 22 Aug 2026 View 2 Im Serious sexual and violent offenders could be confined to small areas just a few miles wide on their release from prison, it's been revealed In a new crackdown, ministers will bring in strict curbs to the freedoms of offenders, with victims having a say in setting the boundaries in which they must stay The move is said to offer victims greater freedom to travel without the fear of unexpectedly coming face-to-face with their offender However, the zones will also ensure offenders can still access vital appointments and services that help to reduce their chances of reoffending The rollout starts in October, and will see GPS monitoring used to track their movements tracked around the clock, allowing probation services to identify breaches and take swift action when the rules are broken - including recalling them to prison

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Piccadilly Gardens revamp and hundreds of flats amongst latest Greater Manchester developments These are the latest significant developments tabled with councils across Greater Manchster Comments News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporter An overhaul of Piccadilly Gardens and hundreds of new flats for the city centre are just two of the latest developments tabled in Greater Manchester Piccadilly Gardens has long been a talking point amongst city dwellers. In the beating heart of Manchester, the area acts as a transport hub, lunchtime eating spot and a place to hang about Now there are plans to give it a complete makeover. The council intends to make it a ‘distinctive green heart’ Elsewhere in the city centre, Gary Neville ’s property company has joined onto a plan to build more than 700 flats. This scheme, on Great Ancoats Street, would see 723 flats spread over two apartment blocks, if approved Here is a breakdown of each borough’s recently submitted public notices…

candidates.evidence_text: True crime series I was alone with an infamous cop killer - I still think about what he did next Retired police officer, Tony Davies, came face to face with Anthony Hughes, who soon after executed Inspector Raymond Codling at Birch Services on the M62 News Lee Grimsditch Features Writer 17:05, 22 Aug 2026 Updated 17:31, 22 Aug 2026 For Tony Davies, it seemed like a routine callout as a police officer in North Wales. He had joined the force at 19 after an unhappy two-year stint in the Merchant Navy But becoming a police officer was different. Working the thin blue line suited him – or, as Tony puts it, he was a "round peg" who found a "round hole". Now 72 and long-retired, he joined the force in the early 1970s and eventually worked his way up to sergeant In the late summer of 1989, Tony found himself heading out to a crime scene after his station in Flintshire received the call about a stolen firearm. "I got called to somebody that nicked a shotgun from the back of a car, and some cartridges, and ran off into the woods," he told After witnesses told him which way the thief had fled, he followed the trail through the woodland until he spotted a figure "There's this guy sitting on a stile, and he's got the gun over his knee and a box of cartridges next to him. I thought, 'There's no way.'

They seized around £100,000 worth of stock from several shops on the high street on Wednesday, August 5 Police said many of the toys were poor-quality and had not been safety tested. Neighbourhood officer for Strangeways, PC Wyatt from GMP's Cheetham Hill neighbourhood team, said: "We want to raise awareness of "People may think they're getting a bargain when purchasing counterfeit toys, but many of these products have not been safety tested. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Strangeways Huge £100k haul of 'poor-quality' toys seized from Strangeways shops "No amount of money saved is worth risking a child's safety" News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter 15:17, 22 Aug 2026 Trading Standards Toy Visits Officers s Greater Manchester Police officers and Trading Standards teams 'acted on intelligence' over shops in the Strangeways area selling suspected counterfeit toys. They seized around £100,000 worth of stock from several shops on the high street on Wednesday, August 5 Police said many of the toys were poor-quality and had not been safety tested. Some of them could have contained 'dangerous chemicals that could cause serious harm' A spokesperson for GMP said more operations are planned across the area as part of the wider operation to target premises involved in illicit trading. Neighbourhood officer for Strangeways, PC Wyatt from GMP's Cheetham Hill neighbourhood team, said: "We want to raise awareness of "People may think they're getting a bargain when purchasing counterfeit toys, but many of these products have not been safety tested. Poor-quality toys can pose choking hazards to children and, in some cases, contain dangerous chemicals that could cause serious harm "We understand that the rising cost of living puts pressure on household budgets, but no amount of money saved is worth risking a child's safety

The judge accepted the prosecution case that baby Victoria died from hypothermia after being exposed to 'significant cold stress' He rejected the defendants’ claims that Victoria was smothered in a 'terrible accident' as they slept in the tent. One passenger who landed shortly after the incident has praised airport staff on how they ‘seamlessly’ handled the situation Shortly after 11.20pm last night, Friday August 21, police were called to the airport after the man 'encroached' onto the airfield. The incident lasted for around 15 minutes, a spokesperson for Manchester Airport said, before he was taken to hospital from the scene It is understood the incident was mental health-related. The airport spokesperson confirmed the incident was resolved with flights now back to normal. A temporary fix has been put in place following the security breach Among the seven flights diverted were a TUI flight from Boa Vista in Cape Verde, which according to Flightradar24 had to be diverted to East Midlands, a Ryanair flight from Agadir in Morocco diverted to Birmingham and an easyJet flight from Barcelona diverted to Liverpool. candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Airport LIVE EVENT ENDED Updated 19 hours ago Manchester Airport security breach RECAP after 7 flights diverted and '17 held' as man gets on airfield Police were called to the airport after a man 'encroached' the airfield Manchester Airport Police were called to the airport just after 11.20pm last night (Friday, August 21) after the man 'encroached' onto the airfield. The incident lasted for around 15 minutes, a spokesperson for Manchester Airport said, before he was taken to hospital from the scene The Manchester Evening News understands the incident was mental health-related. Amid the incident, seven flights due to land at Manchester Airport were diverted elsewhere Some of those included were the TUI flight from Boa Vista in Cape Verde, which according to Flightradar24 had to be diverted to East Midlands, a Ryanair flight from Agadir in Morocco diverted to Birmingham and an easyJet flight from Barcelona diverted to Liverpool Around 17 flights due to arrive at the airport were held. This had a knock-on effect on arrivals and caused delays The airport spokesperson confirmed the incident was resolved with flights now back to normal. A temporary fix has been put in place following the security breach

The 24-year-old was reported missing by her grandmother on February 2, 2022 She was one of the people Alisha was closest to in her young life, with the pair having spent a period of time living together. But she had not heard from Alisha in a couple of weeks and was growing concerned about her Greater Manchester Police issued a public missing person's appeal to try and find Alisha on March 1, 2022. Later that month, the search became a murder investigation, as detectives came to the sad conclusion Alisha had 'come to serious harm' I spoke to Alisha's grandmother outside her Ashton-under-Lyne home in the days following GMP's announcement. She was in shock at the events that were unfolding around her and clearly worried sick about her beloved granddaughter She was also determined to do what she could to try and bring her beloved granddaughter home. She was keen to speak to the Manchester Evening News as part of this, but at the moment we spoke she was expecting a GMP officer to arrive any minute with an update about Alisha

V News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 07:16, 22 Aug 2026 In his darkest of times Tony Wilson was still capable of a good quote. He was fighting for his life after developing renal cancer when he delivered a memorable quip Doctors had suggested he take Sutent. It would not provide a cure but would extend his life. But Manchester Primary Care Trust refused to fund the £3,500 per month cost of the drug. Yet patients alongside him at The Christie Hospital and living in Cheshire did receive funding Music industry and media friends rallied to help pay. Branding the situation a scandal Wilson pointed out that tummy tucks were available on the NHS, and said at the time: " I thought where am I going to find the money? I'm the one person in this industry who famously has never m He never paid for private health care because he was a socialist. Wilson died on August 10th 2007 aged 57 after the cancer progressed and he suffered a heart attack On his Peter Saville designed headstone in Manchester's Southern Cemetery it says: "Broadcaster Cultural Catalyst". His part in Manchester's renaissance from post-industrial gloom was huge

candidates.evidence_text: Monday 13 July 2026 at 3:43pm Play Brightcove video Sarah and husband Martin has been speaking to ITV Granada Reports’ Emma Sweeney A breast cancer patient from Greater Manchester says she’s devastated and angry that a drug that she believes could extend her life is still not available on the NHS in England Sarah Barchetti, who has been living with secondary breast cancer for seven years, has been treated at The Christie hospital in Manchester throughout her illness. But now, as NHS treatment options dwindle, Sarah has turned to fundraising for private care Sarah said: “It blew our world apart,” recalling her diagnosis in 2019 She added: “I’ve lived with it now for seven years. I’m eternally grateful to The Christie, but we’ve come to a point now where they can’t offer me anything else under the NHS. My team are as frustrated as I am.” Sarah believes the drug Enhertu could help her, but while it is available to NHS patients with HER2-low metastatic breast cancer in Scotland, it is not yet offered in England

candidates.evidence_text: Damian Woolfenden, 18, is accused of posting Christchurch attacker Brenton Tarrant's live-streamed video of the 2019 killings on to the self-described "pro-white" platform White Pilled TV Woolfenden, formerly of Bury, Greater Manchester, also allegedly posted the manifesto of far-right terrorist Andres Breivik, who killed 77 people in two attacks in Norway on June 22 2011, on to a Telegram group, the court heard He appeared at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Friday via video link, and spoke only to confirm his name and date of birth Woolfenden has been remanded in custody and will next appear at the Old Bailey on 25 September He is said to have had on his home computer the manifesto of US white supremacist mass shooter Payton Gendron and German neo-Nazi synagogue shooter Stephan Balliet along with a firearms guide The teenager is charged with three counts of publishing threatening written material stirring up racial hatred, one relating to foreigners and one to Jewish people

candidates.what_happened: Manchester's adult services rated 'Good' by Care Quality Commission
candidates.source_evidence: A Care Quality Commission (CQC) inspection report published today (Wednesday 5 August) has found that Manchester City Council’s adult social care services are Good The CQC’s local authority assessment for Manchester, the first of its kind under a new system, scored the Council’s services at 72% - making it the highest rating for any of the England’s biggest cities outside London Adult social care provides support to citizens ranging from young adults to people who are in the later years of their lives. Adult social care works with vulnerable adults who have physical, learning disabilities, and mental health needs Last year (2025/26) 9,937 people received long-term adult social care support, which includes support in people’s own homes, as well as support to people in Care Homes, Extra Care schemes and supported living. candidates.lead: Oldham Council has secured funding to launch the Young Creative Producers Programme (YCPP) to give young people the opportunity to shape the future of culture across the borough

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Council is launching a new licensing scheme for landlords of houses in multiple occupation (HMOs) The scheme is designed to improve property conditions, strengthen management standards, and ensure tenants have access to safe, high-quality accommodation and was agreed at a meeting of Bolton Council’s Cabinet on Monday (August 17) HMOs are properties that are occupied by three or more people from different households, who share at least one basic amenity i.e. a kitchen, bathroom or toilet - the definition includes bedsits, shared houses and some self–contained flats that did not meet the required standard It is unacceptable that landlords cut corners in critical areas such as failing to obtain fire, gas, and electrical safety certificates or ensuring properties are safe Many landlords operate responsibly, but a substantial proportion of HMOs are poorly managed, unsafe and impact on the community In the past three years, the council has received 1,885 complaints about disrepair in rented homes, typically relating to fire safety, electrical and structural defects, overcrowding, cold and damp, and poor waste management and pest control

candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. candidates.evidence_text: Grub on the Docks - Media City UK Street Food Line-Up: Featuring Sizzling Seoul, Dukes Po Boys, and more Grub on the Docks Venue Gardens Dates 28 th May - 20 th Sep '26 Open Tuesday to Sunday weekly, 12 noon – 10pm GRUB on the Docks is bringing the flavour this summer – think unreal street food, ice-cold drinks and non-stop vibes right in the MediaCity gardens, on the waterfront. We’re talking a stacked rotation of indie food like Sizzling Seoul, Umami Cartel, Oppa Korean Dogs and more, switching it up every week so there’s always something new to try. NEW challenge, take on the BELLY BUSTER CHALLENGE from CAFF – sausage. bacon. egg. black pudding. hash brown. All packed into one proper Belly Buster bap for £7.50. Time to beat is 5 minutes set the fastest finishing time and your next Belly Buster is FREE . EVENTS Wine on the Docks Every Wednesday | All day, venue hours Midweek just got better. Every Wednesday, buy two glasses of the same wine and we’ll top up the rest of the bottle on us. No catch, no fuss just a proper reason to make Wednesday your new favourite day. Sunset Sessions Every Friday | 5–8pm Clock off and head straight to the water’s edge. A rotating line-up of DJs kicks off the weekend early, with a trader special and a featured drinks offer to match. Same time, same spot, every Friday, your after-work wind-down sorted. Paws on the Docks 8 AUGUST | 22 AUGUST | 5 SEPTEMBER | 19 SEPTEMBER | Mornings Bring the dog, grab a coffee, make a morning of it. Paws on the Docks is our relaxed dog-friendly social – think breakfast specials, water bowls, complimentary pup cups and market stalls that welcome four-legged visitors as warmly as the two-legged ones. Residents social Thursday 20th August – 5pm to 7pm An evening for all MediaCity residents, with a DJ playing live on the docks. A nice informal social, come down, grab a drink and meet other residents at our waterfront setting. Media Makers Mixer Thursday 27th August – 5pm to 7pm A regular hosted networking event for MediaCity’s creative and production community, designed to bring people together and encourage connections across the area. Be the first in the know Sign up to receive email updates on the latest events, news and offers at MediaCity Visit our privacy policy here. Welcome to The Bolly-woods, where the dancing is non-stop, the drama is bigger than your aunties, and the romance is straight out of a filmi blockbuster! Meet Surinder, sweet, strong, and stuck in a never-ending chore list thanks to her two Insta-fame obsessed stepsisters, Lovely and Bubbly. Her only real support? The one and only Basanti, a cow with the dance skills of Bollywood superstar! Meanwhile, Prince Kavi is drowning in marriage pressure from his royal family. But when he accidentally bumps into Surinder, sparks fly. Enter the fabulous Devi Godmother played by Harpz Kaur (BBC Asian Network, CBBC's Saturday Mash-up). She'll be arriving in full-on glam mode with magic, makeovers, and masala moves. An all singing, all dancing Bollywood revamp of beloved family classic Cinderella With a dazzling Bollywood Ball, a mystical slipper, and a lot of drama, Surinder’s destiny is about to get a serious glow-up! Book your tickets now, before midnight strikes! A delightful blend of storytelling, music, dance and humour. A fine example of the way diversity enriches our culture. Surinderella showcases authentic, joyful visibility and representation Buy direct from venues with ATG Tickets. Transparent booking fees, no late stage surprises. The Palace Theatre of Varieties opened on Whit Monday 1891 and cost its owners the then colossal sum of £40,500. In the late 1970’s the Palace Theatre underwent a major refurbishment and re-opened in 1981 with Andrew Lloyd Webber’s Jesus Christ Superstar and has since then retained its position as the premier provincial touring venue

Hidden in plain sight in Chinatown, it’s the kind of place chefs recommend, food writers praise, and regulars quietly keep going back to Jay Rayner called it “everything it should be” when he visited in 2021, which is about right. It’s intimate, informal, very good value and usually busy enough to make you feel smug if you’ve managed to get a table without waiting The pho is obviously a very good choice. So are the bánh mì. So is most of the menu, to be honest. But for the next Open Fire Dining Club , Pho Cue are stepping out of Chinatown and heading to Torr Vale Mill for something a little different They’ll be joining Tartuffe on 22 and 23 August for a menu that looks at Vietnamese cooking through a few different routes: the French influence that still runs through parts of the cuisine, the traditional use of fire found across Vietnam, and Cue’s more modern approach to Vietn There’s a continuation from the Porta dinner here too. candidates.evidence_text: The £35 million project set within 154 acres has transformed the former site of Worsley New Hall, restoring the historic walled garden, lake and surviving buildings Originally built for the 1st Earl of Ellesmere between 1840 and 1845, Worsley New Hall was a grand Gothic-style mansion, complete with glorious, formal landscaped gardens It’s now one of UK’s must-see gardens with so much to enjoy for visitors of all ages Step inside the magnificent 11-acre Weston Walled Garden, the site’s jewel in the crown. One of the largest Victorian walled gardens in the UK, it showcases a range of growing techniques and edible plants There’s also the spectacular Paradise Garden showcasing exotic planting inspired by Asiatic and Mediterranean gardens. The orchard and nearby bee and butterfly garden, have been designed to attract wildlife The Peel Learning Garden, supported by The Peel Group, will help schoolchildren learn how plants affect our lives and the planet, whilst the Community Wellbeing Garden provides a space for people to garden, socialise and relax

candidates.evidence_text: The award-winning Stockport Foodie Friday will be hosting the Northern heat of the prestigious British Street Food Awards in Stockport Market on Sunday 23rd August, 12pm to 6pm Stockport Foodie Friday regularly attracts thousands of visitors to Stockport on the last Friday of every month and was crowned ‘Best Pop-Up’ at the 2016 Manchester Food & Drink Festival Awards and again in 2022 The event has also secured international recognition, with Foodie Friday nominated for the ‘Best Placemaking’ award at the City Nation Place Awards 2025, competing against entries from Stockholm, Toronto and Cleveland, USA This exciting collaboration with the British Street Food Awards creates the unique opportunity to spend a relaxed Sunday afternoon in Stockport’s beautiful Victorian Market Place, sampling some of the very best street food that the North has to offer. Twenty traders have been sel The judging panel includes BBC Radio Manchester Breakfast Show host Joe McGrath , creator of ‘Filler’ zine Holly Temple and chef Sam Buckley , of acclaimed Stockport restaurant ‘Where The Light Gets In’, which has a Green Michelin Star. They will decide which trader goes forward As well as so many delicious food choices on offer, the event will also feature live music and children’s activities throughout the afternoon making this the ideal family-friendly day out. Visitors are strongly encouraged to come along to eat, drink and vote !

candidates.evidence_text: Chair and BID Director & Leasing Director at Orbit Developments Rhys, has been part of the Orbit team for over 20 years and has spent the last 15years working on a 400,000 square foot of Stockport town centre portfolio which includes offices, retail and business units Orbits involvement in the town centre started in the early 1970’s. Many of the properties under Orbits ownership sit within the BID boundary meaning many of its customers are Levy Payers whilst Orbit themselves are a notable Levy Payer Rhys led Orbits introduction of a town centre reward card for its 3,000+ customer employees and is a strong advocate for the towns independent offer Rhys’ connections to Stockport are not solely through work; he is also a resident of the borough with his young family and was one of the original Stockport Ambassador programme established in 2017 He also sits on the Stockport council of the Greater Manchester Chamber of Commerce and Economic Alliance

candidates.evidence_text: The Science and Industry Museum has unveiled a special Pride programme coinciding with Manchester’s famous celebration of inclusivity this August Spanning talks, newly displayed objects and creative workshops, the Museum’s Pride schedule will kick off on Mon 24 Aug, running through the duration of the festivities until Mon 31 Aug Central to the programme will be a series of Spotlight Talks that explore and celebrate the life and legacy of LGBTQ+ hero Alan Turing. Widely recognised as one of the founding fathers of computer science, Turing’s wartime codebreaking contributions helped save an immeasurable nu Led by the museum’s friendly Spotlight Volunteers in the Revolution Manchester Gallery, these talks will take place Mon 24 Aug and Mon 31 Aug at 1.45pm and 2.45pm, and on Sat 29 Aug at 11.15am, 12.15pm and 1.45pm Alongside the Spotlight Talks, there’ll be opportunities to discover more about Turing’s impact through newly installed objects and stories which will be displayed alongside the iconic Manchester ‘Baby’ computer These include Baiba Auria’s rainbow portrait, which celebrates Turing’s iconic status among the LGBTQIA+ community in Manchester, and a special £50 note featuring the visionary mathematician’s face

This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. The evening kicks off early downstairs at 7pm with a laid-back, candlelit soundtrack of live soul and neo-soul. But as the clock strikes 10pm, the main room transforms into a full-scale celebration as Manchester's finest DJs and live performers spin everything from old-school Lauryn Hill anthems to fresh, bass-heavy tracks from Burna Boy and Drake. The best part? It is completely free entry all night, meaning you can save your cash for the venue's legendary cocktails, private karaoke booths, and retro photo stands. If you happen to miss out on Friday's action, or you simply want to make it a double-header weekend of live music, don't worry - the venue hosts their equally electric sister event, Manchester Got Soul , where the legendary resident house band delivers three incredible live sets of timeless Motown, soul, and rock 'n' roll classics

candidates.title: We will find the new Rodri - Maresca
candidates.summary: The Spain midfielder moved to Barcelona this week after seven years as a key player at the Etihad Stadium. Rodri himself took over from the Brazilian midfielder Fernandinho who was an inspirational figure during his time at City
candidates.reason: Visible repeat policy allows this item: concrete_story_change:declared. | Validator: news item is 739850 days old (hard cutoff 14d), dropped regardless of update wording.
candidates.practical_angle: Официальный клубный источник должен подтверждать время матча и обновления.
candidates.lead: We will find the new Rodri - Maresca
candidates.evidence_text: The Spain midfielder moved to Barcelona this week after seven years as a key player at the Etihad Stadium. Rodri himself took over from the Brazilian midfielder Fernandinho who was an inspirational figure during his time at City. And speaking ahead of our Premier League opener against Bournemouth on Sunday, Maresca says the Club has been consistently successful at replacing great players. “Try to find the new Rodri, it is what it is,” he said when asked about replacing the 2024 Ballon d’Or winner. “Rodri, when he arrived here hadn’t won the Ballon d’Or, the Champions League or the Club World Cup. “When he joined the club and after he achieved many important things. Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri. “I was thinking last night when David Silva was here, [people were] worried, Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. “When Aguero was here, everyone was worried, Erling arrived. Fernandino? Rodri arrived. It’s just about this. “When they leave we need to recruit the next one. Last night I was thinking about that, it’s normal, it’s a change, it’s not a problem go again and try.” Maresca expects more transfer business to be done before the window shuts on 1 September. While the make-up of his squad won’t be entirely clear until then, he did reveal that three Academy players who impressed on the pre-season tour to Asia will remain with the first team squad. “Kaden [Braithwaite], Floyd Samba and Ryan McAidoo are going to be with us. We need around 20 players plus those three players full of energy. We are happy.” He also said that most Premier League clubs are in a similar situation in not knowing how their squads will look. “I think it’s a similar situation for most clubs and fans,” Maresca said. “We are waiting to do things. The normal thing in the transfer window is you have to wait until the last week, because all the clubs try to keep players until the last, so it’s normal. “I’m not worried about that. When the transfer window closes and we have all the squad here, for sure it will be different.” Premier League 2026/27 home tickets now on sale General admission tickets for Manchester City’s home 2026/27 Premier League fixtures are now on sale to Premium, Matchday and Junior Members. Season Ticket Members, meanwhile, are now also able to purchase additional tickets for selected games. Premier League match-by-match ticket prices for junior and adult Matchday Members have been retained at the same rate for a third consecutive season. It promises to be anot

candidates.evidence_text: Football Manchester City FC Doku, Nunes, Marmoush - Man City injury news and return dates before Bournemouth clash Manchester City host AFC Bournemouth at the Etihad Stadium this weekend as Enzo Maresca leads the Blues in the Premier League, for the first time Comments Spor Manchester City are returning to Premier League action this afternoon when they host Bournemouth. The fixture marks the first time Enzo Maresca has led the Blues in the top flight and he is expected to be welcomed warmly by supporters. Ahead of the fixture, City's head coach will Savinho was absent with an illness against Arsenal last weekend. However, he is now on the verge of leaving City and joining Tottenham, so is highly unlikely to feature in today's squad. After the Community Shield defeat, the Blues were also left sweating over the fitness of Jere With this in mind, MEN Sport has rounded up the latest City injury news The Belgian winger started the Community Shield game last week, but was replaced at half-time by Jack Grealish . When he re-emerged to take his spot on the bench, Doku could be seen with an ice pack strapped to his calf. In his pre-match press conference on Friday, Maresca said: Potential return date: September 5 vs Coventry
